payload.reasoning: This hand provides perfect mana for all spells, including a turn 2 Gifted Aetherborn and a turn 4 Moan of the Unhallowed. While 5 lands is a bit high, it ensures smooth play for the first few turns and avoids mana screw, which is generally worse than mana flood on an opening hand, especially on the draw where you get an extra card.

The hand has a good land count (4 lands) for consistent mana. It offers early interaction with Swords to Plowshares and a turn 1 play with Ancestral Blade, followed by a turn 3 Pilgrim of the Ages. This hand is playable and offers a reasonable curve.

This hand has only two lands for a seven-card hand, which is very risky, especially with high-cost cards like Vilis (7 mana), Vogar (6 mana), and Gavony Unhallowed (5 mana). While Reassembling Skeleton is a good early play and Sign in Blood can draw cards, relying on Sign in Blood to find lands when you only have two is too speculative and will often lead to being mana-screwed and unable to cast your powerful threats.

This six-card hand has only one land, making it virtually unplayable. While there's a 1-mana spell, the rest of the hand consists of 3 and 4-mana cards, which will be stuck in hand for multiple turns. Mulling to 5 cards with a scry 2 offers a better chance of finding a playable curve.

This is a 5-card hand after two mulligans, making further mulligans highly detrimental. The hand provides two lands, enabling early interaction with Doom Blade. While Maalfeld Twins is a late-game play and Demonic Embrace lacks an immediate target, the hand has a path to victory if more lands or creatures are drawn. Going to 4 cards would severely reduce the chances of winning.
